title: Veterans Pension — December Cost-of-Living Raise of a Veteran's Social Security Figure in a Benefit Income Statement
content:
# Social Security cost-of-living raise in the Veterans Pension benefit income statement

**Clause.** In a veteran's benefit income statement on his Veterans Pension award, the veteran's Social Security figure is raised according to how long ago its benefit level took effect, counted in whole months from the date the benefit level took effect, as shown on his most recent Social Security report, to the date of the statement — the date the statement carries, the day the change began, and not the day the veteran files it:

| Whole months since the benefit level took effect | Raise applied to the annual figure | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| 24 or more | the two most recent December cost-of-living increases together | multiplied by 1.0537 |
| 12 to 23 | the most recent December increase | multiplied by 1.028 |
| under 12 | none — stated as reported | multiplied by 1 |

The raised figure is rounded to the cent.

## Both sides of each threshold (hypothetical figure of 12000.00)

| Whole months | Stated figure |
|---|---|
| 11 | 12000.00 |
| 12 | 12000.00 multiplied by 1.028, which is 12336.00 |
| 23 | 12336.00 |
| 24 | 12000.00 multiplied by 1.0537, which is 12644.40 |

## Questions answered

*How are two December increases applied?* Together, as the single multiplier 1.0537 on the annual figure as reported.

*Whose figure is this?* The veteran's own Social Security figure — the one he receives in his own name.
